name: Brownish Green
lede: Brownish Green is a modifier on [[green]], recorded by the xkcd 2010 crowd survey, in a color space some languages never bother to separate from blue.

sections.title: A modifier, and a linguistic aside
sections.body:
The name itself is undocumented before 2010 beyond ordinary descriptive use [1]. Philip Ball notes that the Celtic word *glas* covers a range running from a brownish-green to blue, and that Japanese *ao* can mean green, blue or dark depending on context; whether a language draws the line between hues is a matter of vocabulary, not of what its speakers can see [2]. In the 1970s, Michel Pastoureau records designers briefly putting brownish-green military-surplus shades into civilian fashion, a trend that did not last [3].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[mud-green|Mud Green]], only 3.2 units away and read as almost the same color [4]. [[murky-green|Murky Green]] is close too, also read as almost the same color [4]. [[olive|Olive]] sits further out, also brownish, at about 7.7 units [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color appears in 66 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.28 percent, rarer than 52 percent of our named colors, as photographed [5]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, 1.7 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive, and inside a painting it plays an accent in 64 percent of its appearances [5]. The earliest match dates to 1500, 510 years before the xkcd survey; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [5].
